info.title: Capy API
info.description: Programmatic access to Capy's agent platform.

schema.description: Automations in any of these projects.
With `projectId` or `projectIds`: automations in every other project the key can read instead.
Only enabled (true) or only disabled (false) automations. Omit for both.
Automations created at or after this instant.
Automations created before this instant.
Open (the default), closed, or all. `stateIds` narrows further.
The assignee: a user id, a thread id, `me` for the key's own user, or `none`.
The creator: a user id, a thread id, `me` for the key's own user, or `none`.
Issues that mention any of these people: a user id, or `me` for the key's own user. `true` is `me`.
With `mentioned`: issues that mention none of those people instead.
Issues carrying any of these labels.
The sub-issues of this issue code.

Issues due today, tomorrow, this_week (today through Sunday), next_week, this_month (today through the month's end), overdue, or none. Several, and a `dueFrom`/`dueTo` range, match any of them. Dates follow `today`.
Issues due on or after this date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive.
Issues due on or before this date (YYYY-MM-DD), inclusive.
With `due`, `dueFrom` or `dueTo`: issues that match none of them instead.
The caller's local date for `due`; defaults to today's UTC date.
Words in the issue, or an issue number or code.
Exclusive forward event-ID cursor from cursor. Without either bound, returns the oldest page.
Exclusive backward event-ID cursor from beforeCursor. Without after, returns the nearest older page.
Exclusive forward event-ID cursor from cursor. Without either bound, returns the oldest page.
Exclusive backward event-ID cursor from beforeCursor. Without after, returns the nearest older page.
Event-count target, default 50 and maximum 200, paged exactly like the messages list. A page can contain no attachments; continue until its directional cursor is null.
The last `id:` a client read; the committed lane resumes after it.
Exclusive event-ID cursor to start the committed lane after; the Last-Event-ID header wins when both are present.
`run`: close the stream with `done` after the run in progress ends, or at once when the thread is not working.
`subagent`: send each subagent's lifecycle as a `subagent` frame. Defaults to `task`, the original `task` frame.
The last `id:` a client read; the committed lane resumes after it.
Exclusive event-ID cursor to start the committed lane after; the Last-Event-ID header wins when both are present.
`run`: close the stream with `done` after the run in progress ends, or at once when the thread is not working.
The last `id:` a client read; the committed lane resumes after it.
Exclusive event-ID cursor to start the committed lane after; the Last-Event-ID header wins when both are present.
`run`: close the stream with `done` after the run in progress ends, or at once when the thread is not working.
Inclusive window start. Defaults to the start of the current UTC calendar month. The window reaches back at most a year before `to`, or 31 days for `hour`.
Exclusive window end. Defaults to now.
Bucket width, in UTC. Defaults to `day`.
Splits each bucket by `user`, `thread`, or billing `item`; repeat it to combine them (`groupBy=user&groupBy=item`). Absent, each bucket has one total.
Only usage by these user or service-user ids; repeat to pass several.
Only usage in these projects; repeat to pass several. Intersected with the key's project access.
Only usage in these threads and their subagents; repeat to pass several. Threads this key cannot read match nothing.
Only model usage served by these model ids; repeat to pass several.
Rows per page, 1 to 1000. Defaults to 100.
Opaque page token: pass the previous page's `cursor` back with the same window, granularity, grouping, and filters.

WebhookBatchStatus.description: Collecting accepts events; queued has one automation run; cancelled retains scrubbed history without a run.

WebhookBatchGroupValue.description: A non-null finite JSON scalar; string, number, and boolean grouping values remain distinct.

WebhookBatchReason.description: The boundary that closed or cancelled a webhook batch.

body_pointer.description: Strict RFC6901 JSON pointer into the parsed body, up to 1024 characters. Empty selects the root. The selected value must be a non-null finite scalar of at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes when JSON encoded.

equals.description: Expected value, compared as text: a selected string, number, or boolean matches when its plain text form equals this. A missing or non-scalar value never matches.
Expected value, compared as text: a selected string, number, or boolean matches when its plain text form equals this. A missing or non-scalar value never matches.

WebhookRuleCondition.description: A body pointer or request header whose value must equal the expected text.

body_pointer.description: Strict RFC6901 JSON pointer into the parsed body, up to 1024 characters. Empty selects the root. The selected value must be a non-null finite scalar of at most 1024 UTF-8 bytes when JSON encoded.

WebhookGroupSelector.description: One body pointer or request header whose value becomes part of the group key.

allOf.description: 1–4 conditions that must all hold for this rule to apply. Omit to apply to every delivery.

group_by.description: Use all for one pending group under this rule, or 1–4 ordered body/header selectors for a typed tuple key. Only body selectors require JSON; missing or invalid values reject the request rather than sharing a fallback group.

WebhookGroupRule.description: One grouping rule: optional conditions plus the fields that define a group.

allOf.description: 1–8 ordered rules. The first rule whose conditions all hold assigns the delivery's group; groups are scoped per rule. A delivery matching no rule starts its own run immediately.

max_events.description: Close after this many unique accepted events, from 2 to 100. Required; no default.

max_wait_seconds.description: Hard deadline from the first event, from 1 to 3600 seconds. Required; later arrivals never extend it.

quiet_period_seconds.description: Optional idle window after the last unique acceptance, from 1 to 3600 seconds and no greater than maximum wait. Omit to disable idle closing. Duplicates never reset it.

cron.description: Five-field cron expression, e.g. `0 9 * * *` for daily at 09:00.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for the schedule, e.g. `America/New_York`.

event.description: The GitHub event that starts a run.

repositories.description: Full repository names to match, e.g. owner/repo.

branches.description: Branch names to match: a pull request's base branch, or the branch of a push, check, or workflow run.

head_branches.description: Head branch names to match: a pull request's head branch, or the branch a check or workflow run ran on.

authors.description: GitHub login names of the author of the pull request or issue the event is on, not the commenter or reviewer (use actors for those).

labels.description: Match when any of these labels is present; on label_change, the label that was added or removed.

actions.description: Raw event action names to match, e.g. opened, closed.

conclusions.description: Check or workflow conclusions to match, e.g. success, failure.

workflows.description: Workflow display names to match (the yml `name`), not file names.

review_states.description: Review states to match, e.g. approved, changes_requested.

actors.description: GitHub login names of the actor that fired the event: the pusher, commenter, reviewer, or merger.

conditions.description: Filters that narrow which GitHub events start a run. A condition matches when the event matches any of its listed values.

run_when.description: Natural-language gate checked against each event before a run starts; non-matching events are skipped, so keep it to one sentence. To remove the gate, omit this field from the trigger; null is rejected.

event.description: The Slack event that starts a run.

workspaces.description: Slack team ids (T...) to match. Not workspace names. A subscription fills in the organization's connected workspace when omitted.

channels.description: Slack channel ids (C...) to match. Not #channel-names.

threads.description: Parent message timestamps to match: only replies in those threads, never a top-level message.

users.description: Slack user ids (U...) to match: the message author on a message trigger, the person who added the reaction on a reaction trigger.

actors.description: Slack user ids (U...) of the actor that fired the event.

reactions.description: Emoji names without colons to match on a reaction trigger, e.g. eyes or firecracker; a custom workspace emoji is its name.

message_placements.description: Match top-level messages, replies, or both.

message_types.description: Match human messages, bot messages, or both.

include_bots.description: Include messages from bots. Defaults to false.

grouping_window_seconds.description: Seconds to group a burst of messages into one run. Defaults to 0 - no grouping, one run per matched message immediately.

organize.description: How each run's thread lands on the board, applied as the run-as principal when the run creates its thread: pinned, filed into folders, tagged. Null organizes nothing.

pullRequestAuthor.description: Who authors this thread's pull requests on GitHub: `capy` for the Capy GitHub App, `user` for the thread's acting human. Null means the acting human's Git identity preference decides.

environmentVariables.description: Write-only environment variables for this thread and its descendants, encrypted at rest. Commands can read the values and outputs are not masked. A replayed requestId preserves the original variables.

visibility.description: Who can see the thread: `org` for everyone at the organization, `private` for its owner and the people it is shared with. Absent, the owner's own default applies, else the organization's. `private` needs a human owner who may create private work, so a service key must name `authorId`.

pullRequestAuthor.description: Who authors this thread's pull requests on GitHub: `capy` for the Capy GitHub App, `user` for the thread's acting human (the `authorId` member, or the key's creator for a service key). Commits and pushes keep the Git identity preference. Absent leaves the preference in charge; a replayed `requestId` keeps the original value.
Who authors this thread's pull requests on GitHub: `capy` for the Capy GitHub App, `user` for the thread's acting human. Null means the acting human's Git identity preference decides.

description.description: A short public label saying whose Captain this is and what it covers, at most 140 characters of plain text, for attribution and discovery. Null when unset.

brief.description: The Captain's first message from you: what it is for and what to start on. Absent, the Captain greets you and asks.

avatar.description: Absent, the Captain takes the first preset face on a blue background.

authorId.description: The active member of the key's organization who owns the Captain. A Captain needs a human owner, so a service key must name one; a personal key owns it itself when absent. A replayed `requestId` returns the existing Captain unchanged.

path.description: The file the digest was read from: `DIGEST.md`, else `ONGOING.md`, else the Captain's `NOTES.md`. Null before the Captain has written any of them.

markdown.description: The file's text. Null when there is no file, or when the file is binary or larger than 64 KiB.

updatedAt.description: When the Captain's drive last changed.

id.description: A user id for `user`, resolved by `GET /users`, or a thread id for `thread`.

code.description: The thread's reference, such as `SCO-123`; null for a user or a thread the key cannot read.

openBlockerCount.description: Open issues the key can read that block this one.

commentId.description: The comment the file came with; null for a file on the description.

openBlockerCount.description: Open issues the key can read that block this one.

description.description: Markdown. An embedded file appears as `capy-file:<fileId>`, one of `files`.

fileId.description: The `fileId` `POST /files` returned. The file's bytes must already be uploaded.

name.description: The file name shown on the attachment.

stateId.description: A state from `GET /issue-states`. Absent, the organization's default applies.

assignees.description: The whole assignee set, primary first. An empty array leaves the issue unassigned.

parent.description: The parent issue's code, such as `CAP-12`. A sub-issue takes its parent's access.

labelIds.description: The whole label set, by id from `GET /issue-labels`.

visibility.description: `org` for everyone in the project, `private` for the key's user and the issue's assignees. Absent, `org`.

createdAt.description: When the work item was first created, for an import. Absent, now; never in the future.

updatedAt.description: When the work item last changed, for an import. Absent, `createdAt`.

dueAt.description: A date sets the due date; null clears it.

assignees.description: The whole assignee set, primary first. An empty array leaves the issue unassigned.

parent.description: A parent issue code sets the parent; null makes it a top-level issue.

labelIds.description: The whole label set, by id from `GET /issue-labels`.

visibility.description: Applies only to a top-level issue a person created; a sub-issue follows its parent.

replyTo.description: The comment this one answers; replies stay one level deep.

issueCode.description: The sub-issue the event happened on; null for the issue in the path.

from.description: The old value of a title, priority, visibility, or state name change, or the old parent's code.

to.description: The new value of a title, priority, visibility, or state name change, or the new parent's code.

issue.description: The other issue's code for a sub-issue or relation event; null when the key cannot read it.

pullRequest.description: `owner/repo#number` for a pull request link event.

relation.description: How the listed issue relates to the one in the path: `blocks` means the path issue blocks it, `blocked_by` that it blocks the path issue.
`blocks`: the path issue blocks `issue`. `blocked_by`: `issue` blocks the path issue. Two issues hold one relation, so a new one replaces the old.

ref.description: A pull request in the issue's project (`owner/repo#123`, `repo#123`, or its URL), or a thread code or id.

url.description: A presigned GET for the file's bytes. Send it without an Authorization header; the signature is the credential.

stateIds.description: Every state of the organization, in the new order.

moveTo.description: The state the deleted state's issues move to; needed while any issue uses it.

prefix.description: The prefix an admin set; null when the organization uses its default.

effective.description: The prefix issue codes carry now.

prefix.description: One to eight letters; null restores the default.

id.description: The sending thread's or subagent's id, the same id the threads and subagents endpoints take.

relation.description: The sender's relation to this thread: `parent` or `ancestor` owns this subagent, `captain` is the Captain directing this thread, and `peer` is any other thread, including a crew thread messaging its Captain.

sender.description: On user entries another agent sent: the thread or subagent that sent it. Absent on messages a person, an integration, or an automation sent, and on the opening task a parent gives its subagent.

attachments.description: On user entries: the files the message carried. On assistant entries: the files the agent delivered with the message, not every file its turn touched.

references.description: On assistant entries: the Capy Drive files the agent delivered by reference, each with its drive location, path, the drive version at delivery, and the id of its copy in `attachments`.

cursor.description: Opaque exclusive event-ID cursor for after. Stable across compaction. Null when no newer events remain. An unchanged cursor means unsettled messages still block forward paging. Retry after they settle.

beforeCursor.description: Opaque exclusive event-ID cursor for before. Stable across compaction. Null when no older events remain.

files.description: Files to attach, such as screenshots or screen recordings, each uploaded first through `POST /files`. The files together must stay within 2 GiB.

delivery.description: How the message reaches a working thread. `interrupt` (the default) cuts the running step and makes the message the next input; `steer` lands it at the agent's next step with nothing cancelled; `queue` waits until the current work finishes.

clientKey.description: A key you choose for this send, unique per message. A retried send with the same key, from the same key's principal to the same thread, posts nothing new and answers the first send's message id with `deduped: true`.

editOf.description: Resend one of your earlier messages as a new version. The thread resets to that message before the agent reads the new text; the rows after it stay stored and can be switched back to.

switchTo.description: Make this superseded version of an edited message live before the send lands, so the message answers on that branch.

pullRequestAuthor.description: Set the thread's pull request author: `capy` or `user` sets it, null clears it back to the Git identity preference, and absent leaves it unchanged. It applies when the agent picks this message up, so a queued message never changes a pull request opened before it.

name.description: The file name shown on the attachment.

mediaType.description: The file's media type, such as `image/png` or `video/mp4`, 1-255 printable ASCII characters. The PUT must send it as `Content-Type`.

sizeBytes.description: The file's exact size in bytes. The PUT must send it as `Content-Length`.

files.description: The files to upload, at least one and at most 250 MB each. The answer's `targets` come back in this order.

fileId.description: The upload's id. Attach it to a message by passing it in the send's `files`.

url.description: A presigned URL. PUT the file's bytes to it with exactly the declared `Content-Type` and `Content-Length`, and no Authorization header.

id.description: The file's id, the same `file.fileId` a message's `attachments` carry. Pass it to the download endpoint.

title.description: The caption the agent gave the file when it delivered it.

messageId.description: The `id` of the transcript message that carries the file. One file the agent delivered in two messages is listed once per message.

source.description: `user` for a file a person or integration attached to a message, `assistant` for a file the agent delivered.

cursor.description: Opaque exclusive event-ID cursor for after, the same cursor the messages list returns. Null when no newer events remain.

beforeCursor.description: Opaque exclusive event-ID cursor for before. Null when no older events remain.

tier.description: Review tier for this round, including its model, effort, and charge multiplier. Outranks the explicit model and both stored first-review and follow-up defaults. Omitted uses the default for the round's scope.

skipped.description: True when a value exceeds the wildcard limit or a repository is unavailable, so admission skips the rule until it is edited

repositoryCondition.description: Omit to preserve the repository condition, null to clear it, or an object to replace it

skipped.description: True when a pattern is over the wildcard limit, so admission and delivery skip the whole row until it is edited

userId.description: With `groupBy=user`: the acting user or service-user id; null for spend with no acting user.

threadId.description: With `groupBy=thread`: the thread id (subagent spend counts toward its thread), `private` for threads this key cannot read, or null for spend outside any thread.

itemType.description: With `groupBy=item`: `llm` for model usage, `review` for code review, `machine` for machine time, `image` for image generation.

itemId.description: With `groupBy=item`: the model id for `llm`, `review` for `review`, the machine size for `machine`, and the generation endpoint for `image`.

model.description: With `groupBy=item`: the model id for `llm` items; null for every other item type.

currency.description: The currency of every dollar amount in the response.

items.description: Rows ordered by bucket start, then dimensions. A row is omitted when every money and token field is zero. Recent buckets can still change while usage settles and the analytics copy syncs, so re-read them and upsert by `start` and `dimensions`.

anyOf.description: Opaque page token: pass the previous page's `cursor` back with the same window, granularity, grouping, and filters.

cursor.description: Token for the next page; null on the last page.

currency.description: The currency of every dollar amount in the response.

remainingDollars.description: Spendable plan and purchased credit, valued in dollars; not a cash or refundable balance. Negative once overdrawn. Null when the organization has no credit balance or an unlimited grant.

periodStart.description: Start of the current subscription period. Null without a plan; usage windows then default to the UTC calendar month.

periodEnd.description: End of the current subscription period; null without a plan.

bearerAuth.description: An API key created in Capy under Settings → API.
